subject: Post-demo: SableMed integration checklist & routing policy playbook
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: alex.rivera@sablemed.com, eng@sablemed.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SableMed integration checklist & routing policy playbook

Alex / Priya / SableMed eng team —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our demo and architecture discussion so we have a clear owner for each item: 

- Goal: embed Redwood inference into the SableMed triage flow with 100ms p99 latency target for standard queries and a fall-back to cheaper quantized model for batch/rerank tasks.
- Primary integration path: client -> Redwood SDK (server-side) -> model routing policies (hosted/dedicated) -> embeddings + reranker for guideline matching.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Share detailed SDK auth instructions + example token rotation flow (jonas_weber) — EOD Mon 2026-03-08. Attachment: sablemed-integration-checklist.xlsx
2) Confirm which endpoints need structured tool-calls (diagnostic extraction, lab-order link) (sablemed eng / priya) — Reply with list by Tue 2026-03-09.
3) Technical deep-dive on routing policy: latency-first vs cost-first tradeoffs (rishi_malhotra) — scheduled notes inline below.
4) Procurement / contract ask: procurement contact + timeline for security review (ben_carter) — Ben to follow up.

Important constraints you mentioned: HIPAA data flows must stay in US regions, and SableMed would like private VPC option for PHI-heavy routes. We recommend a mixed policy: keep PHI inference on Dedicated or Private with region pinning; route non-PHI to hosted for cost efficiency.

I've attached a network diagram and a short checklist. If that looks right I'll loop in our security engineer to start the SOC2 evidence exchange.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sablemed.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@sablemed.com, priya.shah@sablemed.com
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SableMed integration checklist & routing policy playbook

Jonas — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Structured outputs: we need two tool-calls from the model — (a) Extract patient symptom fields into FHIR-like JSON, (b) Suggest next-steps (order labs / schedule follow-up) where output must include a canonical lab code.
2) Throughput/latency: our initial volume is low (2–3 reqs/sec) but bursty during clinic hours. The 100ms p99 sounds aggressive — is that p99 for tail when using Dedicated? What's typical for a 4k token LLM call?
3) Security: we need an audit log of per-request model selection (which model/version served). Also will need a separate contract clause for data retention.

We can get you a list of endpoints this afternoon. Also looping Priya who will coordinate security and compliance requirements.

—Alex
CTO, SableMed

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: alex.rivera@sablemed.com, eng@sablemed.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SableMed integration checklist & routing policy playbook (technical notes)

Alex — quick technical reply to the latency/throughput and routing questions: 

Summary: 100ms p99 is achievable for short prompts (<512 tokens) on Dedicated pools with optimized kernels and batching controls; for 4k token calls expect p95 in the 300–500ms range depending on model. Key recommendations below.

1) Model routing policy (recommended):
- Policy A (PHI routes): Private/Dedicated only, region pin=us-east-1, high-priority queue, max-batch-size=1, no prefix batching, KV caching disabled for PHI unless you encrypt cache per-tenant.
- Policy B (Non-PHI short queries): Hosted, latency-first, continuous batching allowed, prefix cache enabled, p99 target 150ms.
- Policy C (Rerank / embeddings): Use smaller quantized model for candidate generation + CPU-hosted reranker or a low-cost GPU quantized run for embeddings — route by cost threshold and throughput window.

2) Fallback chain example (simplified):
- primary: gptx-8k-dedicated (low-latency)
- fallback1: gptx-8k-quantized (dedicated cheaper)
- fallback2: gpt-medium-hosted (higher latency but cost-saver)

3) SDK/auth notes: use server-side SDK with short-lived token (rotate every 15 minutes) + key-lookup in your KMS. We can provide an example spring-boot middleware that exchanges your session cookie for a Redwood token; see attached checklist for code snippets.

4) Observability: enable per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown on the console so you can audit model selection. We will include a lightweight webhook that posts model selection events to your audit log if you want.

I'll attach a sample routing JSON in the follow-up (config snippet) and can run a short performance sweep against a 4k-token synthetic workload to give numbers specific to SableMed.

-rishi
Principal, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — I can take procurement and compliance on our side. Short checklist from procurement: 
- Please send us procurement contact and PO process (email + expected PO lead time).
- Security: list of required SOC2 artifacts (we will push our SOC2 pack and a short mapping doc).
- SLA exceptions: if you need a 99.9% p99 SLA for the PHI route we'll need an exception and a short appendix in the contract (attached request form: sla-exceptions-request.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) SableMed sends endpoint list + prioritized routes (by Fri 2026-03-12).
2) Redwood performs a perf sweep on a representative 4k-token workload and returns numbers + suggested default routing JSON (target Tue 2026-03-16).
3) Security exchange: Redwood sends SOC2 pack and audit webhook spec by Thu 2026-03-12.

If that timeline works, can we lock a 30-min follow-up on Wed 2026-03-10 at 11:00 PT to review perf results and routing defaults? I'll send a calendar invite.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0199
